source: Wikipedia: Roger Schank
finding: Schank's 1982 Dynamic Memory is the base of the earliest CBR systems: Kolodner's CYRUS and Lebowitz's IPP. A second edition, Dynamic Memory Revisited, came in 1999.
numbers: Dates only: Schank 1982; CYRUS paper 1983 (Cognitive Science); IPP paper 1983 (Artificial Intelligence).
limits: Encyclopedia summary; MOPs are not mentioned on the page. No performance numbers for CYRUS or IPP were found in sources opened this session.
agent_relevance: Memory organised by episodes with reorganisation on new experience is the ancestor of every LLM case bank below.

source: Wikipedia: Case-based reasoning
finding: CBR began in the early 1980s with Schank's students at Yale. First deployed system was Lockheed CLAVIER (Mark, 1989). First ICCBR was held in 1995.
numbers: Years only.
limits: Page does not describe how CYRUS/IPP reorganised memory (no UNIMEM, MOP, CHEF detail). Gap: the 1980s systems have no published benchmark numbers in what we opened.
agent_relevance: Early systems were never measured the way LLM agents are now, so the modern numbers are the only quantitative guide.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Agent framed explicitly as a case-based reasoner: planner plus tool executor plus a growing Case Bank. Case memory adds a clear gain over the same agent without it.
numbers: DeepResearcher avg: full 66.6 F1/80.4 PM vs w/o CBR 59.9/72.2 (CBR +6.7 F1, +8.2 PM). GAIA val 87.88% Pass@3 (L1/2/3 96.23/90.70/61.54); test 79.40%. SimpleQA 95.0 PM. HLE 24.4 PM (CBR +7.0 PM).
limits: Authors' own results; possible contamination on DeepResearcher sets; answer judged by GPT-4o-mini; GAIA test used the bank built on validation.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that an episodic case bank helps a frozen model, even at modest size.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: number of retrieved cases
finding: Retrieving more cases does not keep helping. Best at K=4, plateau after.
limits: Single benchmark family.
agent_relevance: Retrieve a few cases (about 4), not many. More adds noise.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: parametric vs non-parametric case selection and OOD
finding: A learned Q-function over cases (parametric) beats plain embedding retrieval slightly. Case bank saturates fast. Gains hold out of distribution.
numbers: Iterations 1 to 5: no CBR 78.65 to 84.47; non-parametric 79.84 to 84.85; parametric 80.46 to 85.44. OOD (MuSiQue, Bamboogle, PopQA, 4 cases/query): +4.7 to +9.6 points. Token cost GAIA L1 26k in/4.7k out, L3 121k/9.8k.
limits: Binary rewards only; parametric version simplified to single step; saturation after a few rounds with ~33k examples.
agent_relevance: Case selection by learned utility is a small edge over similarity; the main value is having cases at all.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for RAG in LLMs for Legal QA
finding: Cases as tuples (question, support, entities, answer) with hybrid similarity improve legal answers a little over no retrieval.
numbers: Casebase 2,084 cases; test 32. Cosine similarity of Mistral-7B answer to reference: No-RAG 0.8967; best Hybrid AnglEBERT k=3 full case 0.9141 (+1.94%). Support-only k=1 0.9121. LegalBERT k=1 0.9020/0.9043. Significant vs No-RAG at 95%.
limits: Tiny test set (32). Metric is embedding cosine, not correctness. Synthetic GPT-4-made QA. General AnglEBERT beat domain LegalBERT.
agent_relevance: Structured case fields help retrieval; but the effect size is small and weakly measured.

source: Zhao et al. (2023) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Agent stores trajectories and extracted insights, retrieves similar tasks as few-shot. Task-similarity retrieval matters; random retrieval barely helps.
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct 40.0, random retrieval 42.5, reasoning-similarity retrieval 48.5, ExpeL 59.0. HotpotQA: ReAct 28.0, ExpeL 39.0. Insights-only 50% / retrieve-only 55% on ALFWorld. Transfer HotpotQA to FEVER: ReAct 63, ExpeL 70. Reflexion R3 54.4 vs ExpeL 59.0.
limits: Closed models only (gpt-3.5 act, gpt-4 insights); text only; paper text inconsistent about Reflexion vs ExpeL ordering.
agent_relevance: Both pieces (case retrieval and abstracted rules) help; relevance of the retrieved case is the lever.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Small episodic buffer of self-reflections (1 to 3) improves repeated attempts, but fails where tests are weak or tasks need exploration.
numbers: ALFWorld: +22% absolute over 12 trials; 130 of 134 solved. HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1 prior; MBPP Python 77.1 vs 80.1 (worse); LeetcodeHard 15.0 vs 7.5. starchat-beta no gain (0.26 vs 0.26). WebShop: no significant gain. MBPP test false-positive 16.3% vs 1.4% HumanEval.
limits: Sliding window memory; weak model cannot self-correct; test quality is the bottleneck.
agent_relevance: Matches our G2/G3: memory of failures only works when a real check supplies the failure signal.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) ReasoningBank
finding: Memory stores distilled strategies from both successes and failures, not raw trajectories. Beats no memory, Synapse (raw trajectories) and AWM.
numbers: WebArena SR no-memory / Synapse / AWM / ReasoningBank: Gemini-2.5-flash 40.5/42.1/44.1/48.8; Gemini-2.5-pro 46.7/47.7/47.6/53.9; Claude-3.7-sonnet 41.7/42.6/40.8/46.3. SWE-Bench-Verified flash 34.2 to 38.8, pro 54.0 to 57.4. Steps 9.7 to 8.3.
limits: Self-judged success labels (judge accuracy 72.7%). Mind2Web gains are tiny (3.3 to 4.8). AWM fell below no-memory on Claude (40.8 vs 41.7).
agent_relevance: Distil lessons, include failures, expect modest gains of 4 to 8 points.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: failures and test-time scaling
finding: Adding failed trajectories helps ReasoningBank but hurts AWM. Memory plus extra sampling compounds.
numbers: Shopping, flash: Synapse 40.6 to 41.7; AWM 44.4 to 42.2 (worse); ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7. MaTTS parallel k=1 49.7 to k=5 55.1 (vanilla TTS 52.4). Best-of-5 no memory 42.2, with ReasoningBank 55.1. Judge accuracy sim 70 to 90% gives similar success.
limits: One site subset, one backbone.
agent_relevance: Failure memory only pays if stored as a contrastive lesson, not a raw trace.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induced reusable workflows from past episodes lift web agents, more so under distribution shift. Online induction generalises better than offline.
numbers: WebArena GPT-4: 35.5% vs BrowserGym 23.5% (+51.1% relative), steps 5.9 vs 7.9; gains within ~40 queries. Mind2Web step SR cross-task 45.1 vs 36.2; cross-domain offline 32.6/online 35.5 vs 18.6. Action F1 slightly lower (57.3 vs 60.6).
limits: Online can learn from wrong predictions (LM evaluator); workflows used in only 18.5% of tasks in AS variant; GPT-4/3.5 only; offline+online did not beat online alone (34.1 vs 35.5).
agent_relevance: Generalised episode abstractions (workflows) beat raw episodes when tasks shift.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents (experience-following)
finding: Agents copy the output of the most similar stored experience (experience-following). So bad stored cases propagate, and add-all is harmful.
numbers: Add-all vs fixed 100-record memory: RegAgent 55.48 vs 67.53; EHRAgent 13.05 vs 16.75; AgentDriver 32.32 vs 40.11. Strict (oracle) add: 70.95 / 38.50 / 51.00. Coarse GPT-4o-mini judge add: 63.18 / 26.19 / 36.92. History-based deletion strict: EHR +3.39, CIC-IoT +4.20, RegAgent -1.15. Input-output similarity Pearson r near 1 (RegAgent).
limits: GPT-4o-mini main backbone; four non-general tasks; judge quality decides everything; error-gap numbers only in figures.
agent_relevance: Direct empirical echo of Schank-style indexing risk: store only verified episodes (G2, G3), prune by retrieval utility.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) memory management: record quality
finding: Records that history-based deletion kept were more often correct than deleted ones.
numbers: Correctness retained vs deleted (3 judges): EHRAgent 44.1/49.1/54.8 vs 36.3/32.1/48.2; CIC-IoT 78.9/72.2/86.6 vs 56.7/55.1/61.0. Combined deletion shrinks memory ~4x (EHR 1012 to 248).
limits: Combined deletion lowered accuracy on RegAgent (-4.37) and AgentDriver (-1.03).
agent_relevance: Retrieval-count utility is a usable free quality signal for case-base maintenance.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents
finding: Episodic memory stream scored by recency, importance, relevance, with periodic reflections, is needed for believable behaviour. Memory retrieval fails and embellishes.
numbers: TrueSkill: full 29.89, no reflection 26.88, no reflection+planning 25.64, human crowdworker 22.95, no memory/reflection/planning 21.21. Kruskal-Wallis H(4)=150.29 p<0.001; Cohen d 8.16 (N=100 raters). Recency decay 0.995; reflection when summed importance >150. Awareness of party 4% to 52%. 6 of 453 responses hallucinated (1.3%).
limits: Believability, not task accuracy; failures: retrieval misses, embellishment, atypical venues as memory grew.
agent_relevance: A scored episodic stream is the same idea as MOP indexing, with importance as a learned-free weight.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: Skill library of verified code programs retrieved by description embedding (top-5). Removing it stalls progress and slows new tasks.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 iterations, 3.3x more than baselines. Tech-tree 15.3x/8.5x/6.4x faster (wood/stone/iron). Zero-shot Diamond Pickaxe 19 +/- 3 iterations with library vs 36 (2/3 successes) without. No self-verification: -73% items. Random curriculum: -93%.
limits: Needs GPT-4 (GPT-3.5 gives 5.7x fewer items); curriculum hallucinates items; 4-round retry cap.
agent_relevance: Memory entries that were executed and verified are the safest kind of case.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Explicit 4R CBR loop over Kaggle-style cases. Removing CBR is the worst ablation. More than one retrieved case hurt.
numbers: Dev stage: GPT-4 100% success, avg best rank 1.5 vs ResearchAgent 5.4. Ablation avg best rank: full 2.08, w/o ReviseRank 2.58, w/o CBR 3.41. Deployment one-pass: GPT-4 near 100%, GPT-3.5 85%, best baseline 56 to 60%; Mixtral 6% to 31%. Cost per task fell 91.5 to 92.5% from dev to deploy (GPT-4 1.60 to 0.135 dollars).
limits: 12 dev and 18 deploy tasks only; closed models; no limitations section.
agent_relevance: Retrieval with re-ranking by past utility beats plain similarity; use one good case.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) Rememberer: LLMs as semi-parametric RL agents with experience memory
finding: Experience memory with Q-values on each record, updated by Q-learning, no weight updates. Needs few tasks to learn.
numbers: WebShop success 0.39 vs ReAct 0.36 vs LLM-only 0.29 (std 0.02 vs 0.06). WikiHow 0.93 vs 0.89. Used 10 training tasks (~74 steps) vs RL baseline 10,587 tasks. Ablation WikiHow: no discouraged actions 0.81, no observation similarity 0.87, no task similarity 0.94.
limits: Gains small (+3 to +4 points); saturates; LLM Q-estimate abs error 0.417.
agent_relevance: Observation similarity mattered more than task similarity: index by situation, not by label.

source: Dynamic Cheatsheet (2025) Test-time learning with adaptive memory
finding: A curated, rewritten text memory improves some tasks hugely and others not at all. Storing full history can hurt.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 23.3 to 50.0 (DC-Cu); AIME 2025 6.7 to 36.7. GPT-4o Game of 24 10.0 to 99.0 (DC-RS). Full-history GPT-4o AIME 2024 13.3 vs baseline 20.0. GPT-4o-mini AIME 2024 16.7 to 13.3 (worse). GPQA-Diamond GPT-4o 57.1 to 57.1. Tokens 370 (BL) to 1,831 (DC-Cu).
limits: 30-question sets (3.3 points per item); small and reasoning models gain little or regress; model abbreviates memory when rewriting; sequential only.
agent_relevance: Curated memory beats raw-history memory; gains depend on model strength and task having reusable tricks.

source: Mem0 (2025) Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
finding: Extracted-fact memory nearly matches full context at far lower cost, but trails it.
numbers: LOCOMO LLM-judge overall: full-context 72.90, Mem0g 68.44, Mem0 66.88, Zep 65.99, best RAG 60.97, LangMem 58.10, OpenAI 52.90, A-Mem 48.38. p95 latency 17.1s full vs 1.44s Mem0. Tokens 26k vs 1.76k per query. Temporal: OpenAI 21.71 vs Mem0g 58.13.
limits: Authors' own system; 10 conversations; adversarial category dropped; A-Mem re-run.
agent_relevance: Memory still loses 4 to 6 points to just reading everything; compression has a price, especially for time.

source: Hu et al. (2025) MemoryAgentBench
finding: Independent test: elaborate memory agents lose to plain long context or BM25 on most competencies, and all fail at selective forgetting with multi-hop.
numbers: 2,071 questions. Overall: GPT-5-mini long context 60.6, GPT-4o 48.8, BM25 41.5, HippoRAG-v2 41.6, MemGPT 28.3, MIRIX 26.2 (37.7 with GPT-4.1-mini), Mem0 21.1, Cognee 20.6, Self-RAG 18.7. Selective forgetting multi-hop at most 28%. o4-mini FactConsolidation 80.0 at 6K to 14.0 at 32K.
limits: Only a few memory agents tested; budget limited; FactConsolidation only 6K and 32K validated.
agent_relevance: Episodic memory machinery that reorganises (consolidates) is the weak part; updating beliefs when new cases contradict old ones fails.

source: Hatalis et al. (2025) Review of CBR for LLM agents
finding: Maps 4R onto LLM agents: embedding retrieval, LLM as adaptor, utility-threshold retention. Authors say there are no benchmarks for CBR-augmented agents.
numbers: Only number reported: DS-Agent GPT-4 100% dev success, 99% deploy one-pass. Others (Sourati 2023 fallacies, Wilkerson 2024 triage, Dannenhauer 2024 code few-shot) reported without figures.
limits: Mostly theory; no mention of CYRUS or MOPs; citations partly unclear.
agent_relevance: The field itself says the evidence is thin; do not over-trust headline claims.

source: Hua et al. (2024) Case-based or rule-based: how do transformers do the math?
finding: Transformers trained on arithmetic behave like case matchers, not rule users. Accuracy collapses on a held-out region.
numbers: Leave-Square-Out (441 held-out samples): Llama-2-7B base-9 addition 30.2% vs 92% on random split. GPT-2 over 98% random but a hole in the held-out square. In-context similar examples beat random ones (p<0.001); zero-shot base addition 8.8%. Rule-Following Fine-Tuning: GPT-3.5 over 95% on 12-digit addition from 100 samples; Llama-2-7B 91.1% on 9 digits.
limits: Small trained-from-scratch models; fine-tuned pretrained Llama showed no clear holes; prompting/CoT not tested. Author names unverified.
agent_relevance: Models are already case-matchers: nearest-case retrieval fits their nature, but a stored case cannot replace a rule where the case is far.

source: Cross-source synthesis: how many cases
finding: Three independent agent studies find that a small number of retrieved cases beats many.
numbers: Memento best K=4 (64.5 F1) vs K=32 63.9; DS-Agent: more than one example case degraded results; CBR-RAG best k=3 (0.9141) vs k=1 0.9074. Mem0 RAG used k up to 2 only.
limits: Different tasks and metrics; synthesis by this agent, not a single experiment.
agent_relevance: Default to 1 to 4 retrieved cases; test before raising.

source: Cross-source synthesis: memory vs just reading context
finding: Context-reading often matches or beats a retrieval memory when the whole history fits; memory pays when it holds distilled lessons across tasks.
numbers: Mem0 full-context 72.90 vs memory 66.88; MemoryAgentBench long-context 48.8 to 60.6 vs agentic memory 18.7 to 37.7; Dynamic Cheatsheet full history AIME 2024 GPT-4o 13.3 vs curated 40.0.
limits: Synthesis; tasks differ.
agent_relevance: Keep memory for distilled lessons and verified skills, not for transcripts.

source: Cross-source synthesis: where case memory fails
finding: Gains vanish or reverse with weak backbone, bad stored cases, or weak checks.
numbers: Reflexion starchat-beta 0.26 to 0.26; DC GPT-4o-mini AIME 2024 16.7 to 13.3; AWM on Claude 40.8 vs 41.7 no-memory; add-all memory 55.48 vs 67.53 fixed; Reflexion MBPP 77.1 vs 80.1.
limits: Synthesis across opened papers.
agent_relevance: Gate writes on a real check; do not add unverified episodes (matches G2/G3).

source: Synthesis: schema fit
finding: What early CBR memory ideas survive in modern loops: index by situation features, generalise repeated episodes into abstractions, store failures with their cause, prune low-use cases.
numbers: ExpeL insights+retrieval 59.0 vs either alone 50 to 55 (ALFWorld); Rememberer observation-similarity ablation 0.87 vs 0.93; ReasoningBank failure memory +3.2 points.
limits: Design inference, not a measured claim. Several results rely on LLM judges.
agent_relevance: Add a code-gated case store: write only after a held-out check passes, retrieve at most 4, index by observation features, drop never-retrieved cases.
